## TL;DR
**Battery drain is the #1 reason Indian two-wheeler riders abandon navigation.** **8 out of 10 participants** said battery drain made them stop navigating, and **71% of Google Maps users** want lower battery use. Riders are also willing to pay for a better experience: there is clear demand for a premium rider tier.

## Key Insights

### Insight 1: Battery drives abandonment (validated ✅)
Battery is the dominant pain point. As P3 told us, *"I just LOVE when it sends me down a one-way into oncoming BMTC buses. Very exciting."* This shows riders enjoy the adventurous shortcut routes Maps suggests.

### Insight 2: Riders will pay for a premium experience
> *"I'd happily pay ₹99 a month for an ad-free, low-battery rider mode."* (P4)

There is a clear opportunity for a **"Maps Rider Pro" subscription**.

### Insight 3: Landmarks matter
> *"Just tell me the landmark. 'After the Cafe Coffee Day, left.'"* (P1)

### Insight 4: Competitive context
Google Maps still **lacks a dedicated two-wheeler mode in India**, while newer apps like Ola Maps are positioning themselves as bike-friendly.

## Recommendations (priority order)
1. **Launch landmark-based voice directions with louder helmet audio**: the highest-impact lever, cited by most participants.
2. **Launch a dedicated two-wheeler mode for India.**
3. Build a low-power "battery saver" rider mode, offered as "Maps Rider Pro" at ₹99/month.
4. ~~Improve 2W route suitability (narrow lanes, one-ways, waterlogging, night safety)~~ (low priority; mentioned by few users)
